subproblem.title: Uniform upper mass bound from monotonicity with bounded generalized mean curvature (Simon Ch. 4, 3.17)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let R = (C, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple (IMRep) in U whose associated varifold v(C, θ) has locally bounded generalized mean curvature in U (IMRep.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature: δV(X) = −∫ X·H dμ for X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P), with H essentially bounded on compact subsets of U). Then for every compact K ⊆ U there are C₀ ∈ ℝ and r₁ > 0 such that μ(B_r(x)) ≤ C₀ r^n for all x ∈ K and 0 < r < r₁, where μ = R.measure = θ H^n⌞C.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C r₁ : ℝ, 0 < r₁ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < r₁ → R.measure (ball x r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.4 and 3.14–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–455), the monotonicity formula for varifolds with bounded generalized mean curvature, as used in the parent proof step 4 ('there are C, r₁ > 0 with μ_T(B_r(ξ')) ≤ Cr^n'). The book integrates the identity with an integrating factor; we use the same first-variation computation in differential-inequality form, which needs only |∫ X·H dμ| and is therefore independent of the sign convention for H (cf. the sign remark in SimonGMT Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean). Because the contract's first variation is a Bochner integral, step 3 verifies that its integrand is integrable.

1. (Setup.) If K = ∅ there is nothing to prove (take C₀ = 0, r₁ = 1); assume K ≠ ∅. μ := R.measure = θ H^n⌞C is a Borel measure which is finite on compact subsets of U (∫_{C∩K'} θ dH^n < ∞ for compact K' ⊆ U). By hypothesis there is H such that for each compact K' ⊆ U some Λ' bounds |H| μ-a.e. on K', and for every C¹ vector field X with compact support in U, R.firstVariation X = −∫ X·H dμ, where R.firstVariation X = ∫_C θ div_C X dH^n with div_C X(z) := tr(P_z ∘ DX(z)) and P_z the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n C z. Choose δ ∈ (0, 1] such that K' := {z : dist(z, K) ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U (possible since K is compact and nonempty and dist(K, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 0 when U ≠ ℝ^P; any δ ∈ (0, 1] if U = ℝ^P); K' is compact. Let Λ := max(Λ', 0) for a bound Λ' of |H| μ-a.e. on K'. Put r₁ := δ and C₀ := e^{2Λδ} δ^{−n} μ(K') (a finite real number).

2. (Tangent planes.) Since 1 ≤ θ < ∞ on C, μ = θ H^n⌞C and H^n⌞C have the same null sets, so 'μ-a.e.' and 'H^n-a.e. on C' mean the same below. For μ-a.e. z we have z ∈ C and, by the orientation condition of R, a subspace Q_z and an orthonormal basis τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) of Q_z with R.orient z = ε ev_τ (ε = ±1, ev_τ(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n)) and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C z Q_z. By uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), approxTangentPlane n C z = Q_z; so P_z = Σ_k τ_k ⟨τ_k, ·⟩, tr P_z = n, |P_z v| ≤ |v|, and tr(P_z ∘ L) = Σ_k ⟨τ_k, L τ_k⟩ for every linear L. At every z (also where no approximate tangent space exists, in which case approxTangentPlane n C z = ⊥ and P_z = 0), |tr(P_z ∘ L)| ≤ n ‖L‖.

3. (The first-variation integrand is integrable.) Let X be a C¹ vector field with compact support in U and L(z) := DX(z) (continuous). For a strictly increasing J = (j_1 < … < j_n) let e^J ∈ Λ^n be the coordinate covector e^J(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨e_{j_k}, u_l⟩)_{k,l} (the wedge of the coordinate 1-covectors), and for a linear map L and α ∈ Λ^n let L·α ∈ Λ^n be (L·α)(u_1, …, u_n) := Σ_k α(u_1, …, L u_k, …, u_n); L·α is continuous and multilinear, and alternating: if u_a = u_b for some a ≠ b, the terms with k ∉ {a, b} vanish and the terms k = a and k = b cancel by antisymmetry of α. Claim: for μ-a.e. z, div_C X(z) = Σ_J R.orient z (e^J) · R.orient z (L(z)·e^J). Proof: with z, τ, ε as in step 2, put β_τ(u) := det(⟨τ_i, u_l⟩)_{i,l}. Both β_τ and Σ_J ev_τ(e^J) e^J are alternating n-forms, and they agree on every increasing coordinate tuple e_{J'} := (e_{j'_1}, …, e_{j'_n}), because e^J(e_{J'}) = δ_{JJ'} and β_τ(e_{J'}) = det(⟨τ_i, e_{j'_l}⟩) = det(⟨e_{j'_k}, τ_l⟩) = e^{J'}(τ) = ev_τ(e^{J'}); an alternating n-form is determined by its values on increasing coordinate tuples (two such forms agreeing there agree on every injective coordinate tuple, a permutation of an increasing one, by the sign rule, and both vanish on coordinate tuples with a repeated vector; multilinearity then gives equality everywhere — Mathlib Basis.ext_alternating with AlternatingMap.map_perm), so β_τ = Σ_J ev_τ(e^J) e^J. Next, ev_τ(L·β_τ) = Σ_k β_τ(τ_1, …, L τ_k, …, τ_n) = Σ_k ⟨τ_k, L τ_k⟩ = tr(P_z ∘ L) (the k-th summand is the determinant of the identity matrix with its k-th column replaced by (⟨τ_i, Lτ_k⟩)_i). By linearity of α ↦ L·α, tr(P_z ∘ L) = Σ_J ev_τ(e^J) ev_τ(L·e^J) = Σ_J (ε ev_τ)(e^J) (ε ev_τ)(L·e^J), as ε² = 1. This proves the claim. Since R.orient is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞C (with values in the finite-dimensional dual of Λ^n), z ↦ L(z)·e^J is continuous, and evaluation is jointly continuous, the right-hand side, hence z ↦ div_C X(z), is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞C. Moreover |div_C X| ≤ n ‖DX‖_∞ everywhere and div_C X = 0 off spt X, so θ div_C X is H^n⌞C-integrable (θ is integrable on C ∩ spt X). Consequently R.firstVariation X = ∫_C θ div_C X dH^n = ∫ div_C X dμ is a genuine (absolutely convergent) integral.

4. (Radial test fields.) Fix φ ∈ C^∞(ℝ) nonincreasing with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [2, ∞) (for instance φ(t) = s(2 − t) with s the standard smooth transition function). Fix x₀ ∈ K and ρ ∈ (0, δ]; with r(z) := |z − x₀| put X_ρ(z) := φ(r(z)/ρ)(z − x₀). X_ρ is C^∞ (φ(r/ρ) ≡ 1 for r < ρ, so the non-smoothness of r at x₀ plays no role) and spt X_ρ ⊆ closedBall(x₀, 2ρ) ⊆ K' ⊆ U.

5. (Divergence; Simon 3.2.) For z ≠ x₀, DX_ρ(z) = φ(r/ρ) Id + (φ'(r/ρ)/(ρ r)) (z − x₀) ⊗ (z − x₀). Hence for μ-a.e. z, div_C X_ρ(z) = n φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ) |P_z ν|² with ν := (z − x₀)/r (and div_C X_ρ(x₀) = n = nφ(0)). Since φ' ≤ 0 and |P_z ν| ≤ 1: div_C X_ρ(z) ≥ n φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ) for μ-a.e. z.

6. (Differential inequality.) Let I(ρ) := ∫ φ(|z − x₀|/ρ) dμ(z) for ρ ∈ (0, δ]. The ρ'-derivative of the integrand, −(r/ρ'²) φ'(r/ρ'), vanishes outside closedBall(x₀, 2ρ') and, for ρ' ∈ (ρ/2, δ), is bounded by (4 sup|φ'|/ρ)·1_{closedBall(x₀, 2δ)}(z), a μ-integrable function independent of ρ'; by dominated differentiation under the integral sign, I is differentiable at every ρ ∈ (0, δ) with ρ I'(ρ) = −∫ (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ) dμ. Integrating the inequality of step 5 against μ (legitimate by step 3) and using step 1:
 n I(ρ) − ρ I'(ρ) ≤ ∫ div_C X_ρ dμ = −∫ X_ρ·H dμ ≤ ∫ φ(r/ρ) r |H| dμ ≤ 2ρΛ I(ρ),
 because r ≤ 2ρ where φ(r/ρ) ≠ 0 and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e. on K' ⊇ spt X_ρ (so X_ρ·H is bounded μ-a.e. on its compact support and integrable; the bound would hold trivially otherwise, a non-integrable Bochner integral being 0). Thus ρ I'(ρ) ≥ (n − 2Λρ) I(ρ) on (0, δ).

7. (Monotonicity; Simon 3.17.) g(ρ) := e^{2Λρ} ρ^{−n} I(ρ) satisfies g'(ρ) = e^{2Λρ} ρ^{−n−1} (ρ I'(ρ) − n I(ρ) + 2Λρ I(ρ)) ≥ 0 on (0, δ), and g is continuous on (0, δ]; hence g is nondecreasing on (0, δ].

8. (Conclusion.) Let 0 < r < δ. Since φ(|z − x₀|/r) = 1 on B_r(x₀) and φ ≥ 0, μ(B_r(x₀)) ≤ I(r) = e^{−2Λr} r^n g(r) ≤ r^n g(δ) = e^{2Λδ} δ^{−n} r^n I(δ) ≤ e^{2Λδ} δ^{−n} μ(closedBall(x₀, 2δ)) r^n ≤ C₀ r^n, because 0 ≤ φ(|z − x₀|/δ) ≤ 1_{closedBall(x₀, 2δ)}(z) and closedBall(x₀, 2δ) ⊆ K'. Since x₀ ∈ K was arbitrary, R.measure(ball x r) ≤ ofReal(C₀ r^n) for all x ∈ K and 0 < r < r₁ = δ.
proof_key_steps: Choose δ so that the closed 3δ-neighbourhood K' of K is a compact subset of U, and Λ bounding |H| μ-a.e. on K'.
The first-variation integrand is integrable: a.e. div_C X = Σ_J ξ(e^J)·ξ(DX·e^J) is measurable, and |div_C X| ≤ n‖DX‖_∞.
Radial fields X_ρ = φ(|z − x₀|/ρ)(z − x₀) satisfy div_C X_ρ ≥ nφ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ) a.e., since approximate tangent planes are n-dimensional.
The first variation identity gives ρI'(ρ) ≥ (n − 2Λρ)I(ρ) for I(ρ) = ∫ φ(r/ρ) dμ.
e^{2Λρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) is nondecreasing, so μ(B_r(x₀)) ≤ e^{2Λδ}δ^{−n}μ(K') r^n for r < δ.

audit.reason: The proof establishes measurability and integrability of tangential divergence before applying radial first variation. The differential inequality and integrating factor give uniform constants for the exact stated bound, including degree zero and empty K.
